title: Probe Curation — Orthogonality Notes
body:
Goal:
This is a working notebook for building probe sets that are maximally orthogonal across common prompt axes (style, instruction framing, context length, exemplar polarity). The intent: create compact, high-information few-shot banks that reveal distinct failure modes and limit conflation in aggregated evals.

Design principles (working):
- Orthogonality = low cross-correlation of model outputs when varying a single axis. Want probes that isolate effects.
- Compactness: no more than 8 probes per axis for quick runs.
- Human-readable labels for each probe (helps triage).
- Track meta-features: token-length, vocab-coverage, punctuation density, presence of named entities.

Immediate experiments to run:
1) Axis matrix run: style x exemplar-polarity x context-length x temperature sweep (0.0, 0.2, 0.7)
   - For each cell, 10 prompts, 3 seeds, record top-1 and ranked-token perplexity where available.
2) Adversarial prefix insertion: prepend rare-token sequences and measure drift from baseline.
3) Few-shot order sensitivity: permute exemplars and measure label-consistency.

Probe examples (canonical templates)
- Instruction-forward (concise):
  "You are an assistant. Extract the action items from the notes below. Notes:\n  [NOTES] -> Return a bullet list of actions, one per line."

- Instruction-rich (conversational):
  "Help me turn these meeting points into clear, prioritized action items with owners and deadlines. Meeting notes:\n  [NOTES] -> Format: - Action — Owner — Due"

- Exemplar polarity pair (few-shot):
  "Example 1:\n  Q: 'The server crashed after the deploy. Who do we ping?'\n  A: 'Oncall (Alice) — Restart orchestration, follow incident playbook.'\n\n  Example 2:\n  Q: 'We need to speed up tokenizer. Any ideas?'\n  A: 'Profile tokenization hotspots, try fused BPE kernels.'\n\n  Prompt:\n  Q: '[NEW_PROMPT]'\n  A:"

- Ambiguous instruction probe (to trigger hallucination):
  "Summarize what happened in the system. Use whatever details you think are relevant."
  (Expect: model may hallucinate specifics; we flag named entities & invented metrics.)

Failure cases to log (schema for rows in experiment CSV):
- probe_id, axis, seed, temp, prompt_text, exemplar_set_id, token_len, n_entities_extracted, hallucination_flag (yes/no), factuality_notes, top_response_tokens

Measurement heuristics (initial):
- Orthogonality score: 1 - mean_pairwise_cosine(similarity of average-token-distribution vectors) across probes in an axis. (High is good.)
- Stability: fraction of identical high-level labels across seeds / temps.
- Hallucination heuristic: presence of OOV named entities (compare against source doc entity list).
- Instruction adherence: BLEU-like overlap on required fields (for structured outputs).

Quick probe bank (examples, label format: LABEL — brief)
1) CONCISE_EXTRACT — short imperative with explicit output format
2) CHAT_TONE — chatty, persona-driven instruction ("you're a friendly product manager")
3) FORMAL_SUM — formal editorial summary request (longer context)
4) LOW_CONTEXT_AMBIG — one-line ambiguous ask (likely to hallucinate)
5) NEG_EXEMPLARS — few-shot examples that show negative/incorrect answers intentionally (test trust calibration)
6) NUMERIC_PROMPT — asks for counts/percentages (tests numeric hallucination)
7) TOKEN_PADDED — same semantics but with low-value token padding prefix (tests tokenization sensitivity)
8) ENT_NAME_SWAP — identical prompt but entity names swapped to rare tokens (tests memorization)

Example few-shot set (for ACTION_EXTRACTION task)
- Exemplar A (positive):
  Notes: "Deployed service X, found a bug in login flow. Reassign to backend. Follow up 2d."
  Output: "- Assign to backend (Dev: Raj) — Investigate login bug — Due 2d"

- Exemplar B (negative/contradict):
  Notes: "Minor UI polish, no action."
  Output: "- No action needed"

- Test prompt: Notes: "Rolling back release after 5% error increase; notify infra and audit logs"
  Expected behavior: extract 2 actions (rollback, notify infra) + owner suggestions.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to fairly compare orthogonality across different model sizes? (normalize by base entropy?)
- Should we include token-level perturbations (byte-level) or stick to semantic variants?
- Build automatic exemplar selector that maximizes within-axis variance while minimizing cross-axis covariance. Draft algorithm: greedy maximize determinant of exemplar feature matrix, prune correlated items.
- Decide reporting dashboard: heatmap of orthogonality x failure-rate.

Notes-to-self:
- Keep probe text < 300 tokens where possible to avoid long-run costs.
- Use sandbox cluster (dev-dedicated1) for high-temp runs. Tag runs with PROBE-ORTHO-YYYYMMDD for traceability.

Log snippet (quick manual run, 2025-01-16):
- Model: open-llama-65B-quant
- Probe: TOKEN_PADDED
- Temp: 0.2
- Seed: 42
- Observations: padding with repeated "<zz>" tokens increased likelihood of truncating named entities; overall label-stability dropped from 0.84 -> 0.61.
- Action: add ENT_NAME_SWAP before TOKEN_PADDED to measure interaction.

Contact notes: Leo will add entity list extractor; Nina is curating negative exemplars. Plan a brief sync on 2025-02-05 to align metrics.

If this yields clean orthogonal probes we can:
- Publish a short internal guide: "How to build orthogonal probes for prompt banks"
- Add curated probe sets to the prompt-lab repo (small JSON manifest + tags)

End notebook—more iterations incoming.
